description: Illustrative Sunday Mass in Ordinary Time; baseline with deacon and servers.
units: Positions use the canonical 1000 x 830 floor plan; duration is animation seconds, not real liturgical timing.
referenceStatus: Inherited references are not independently checked against an approved Missal.

steps.title: Entrance Procession
steps.text: When the people are gathered, the Priest and ministers go to the altar while the Entrance Chant is sung. The thurifer goes first with a smoking thurible. Next comes a minister carrying the cross, between two ministers with lighted candles, then the lector. The Deacon carries the Book of the Gospels slightly raised, and the Priest comes last.

steps.title: Reverence to the Altar
steps.text: At the altar the Priest, the Deacon and the ministers make a profound bow. The cross bearing the figure of Christ crucified is set up near the altar, and the candles are placed by it. The Deacon lays the Book of the Gospels on the altar. Then the Priest and Deacon venerate the altar with a kiss.

D: lays the Book on the altar

steps.title: Incensing the Cross and Altar
steps.text: If incense is used, the Priest puts some into the thurible and blesses it with the Sign of the Cross, saying nothing. He incenses the cross, then walks around the altar incensing it.

steps.title: Sign of the Cross
steps.text: The Priest goes to the chair. When the Entrance Chant has ended, the Priest and the faithful, all standing, make the Sign of the Cross. The Priest, facing the people, says the words and the people answer "Amen."
say: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

steps.title: Greeting
steps.text: The Priest extends his hands and greets the people, using one of the formulas given. The people reply.

steps.title: Penitential Act
steps.text: The Priest invites the faithful to the Penitential Act, and a brief silence follows. All then make a common confession. The Priest gives the absolution, which lacks the efficacy of the Sacrament of Penance.
say: I confess to almighty God… (all strike the breast)
May almighty God have mercy on us, forgive us our sins, and bring us to everlasting life.

steps.title: Kyrie
steps.text: The Kyrie invocations follow, unless they were already part of the Penitential Act.

steps.title: Gloria
steps.text: When it is prescribed, the Gloria is then sung or said. This applies to Sundays outside Advent and Lent, to solemnities and to feasts. The Priest or a cantor may begin it, or all may begin it together.
say: Glory to God in the highest…
♪ …and on earth peace to people of good will… ♪

steps.title: Collect
steps.text: With hands joined, the Priest says "Let us pray," and all pray in silence for a while. Then the Priest extends his hands and says the Collect. At its end the people acclaim "Amen." A server may hold the Missal.
say: (the Collect of the day) …through our Lord Jesus Christ…

steps.title: First Reading
steps.text: The lector goes to the ambo and reads the First Reading while all sit and listen. At the end the lector acclaims "The word of the Lord," and all reply. A brief silence for meditation may follow.
say: A reading from the Book of…

steps.title: Responsorial Psalm
steps.text: The psalmist or cantor sings or says the Psalm at the ambo, and the people make the response.

steps.title: Second Reading
steps.text: If there is a Second Reading, a lector reads it from the ambo as before, ending with the same acclamation.
say: A reading from the Letter of Saint Paul…

steps.title: Gospel Acclamation & Blessing of the Deacon
steps.text: All rise and sing the Alleluia, or the chant the season requires. If incense is used, the Priest puts some into the thurible. The Deacon bows profoundly before the Priest and asks for the blessing in a low voice; the Priest blesses him in a low voice. The Deacon takes the Book of the Gospels from the altar. Preceded by the thurifer and the candle-bearers, he carries it to the ambo.

steps.title: The Gospel
steps.text: At the ambo the Deacon greets the people with hands joined. As he announces the Gospel he signs the book with his thumb, then signs himself on the forehead, lips and breast, and all do the same. He incenses the book and proclaims the Gospel. At the end he kisses the book, saying a prayer quietly.
say: A reading from the holy Gospel according to N.
Praise to you, Lord Jesus Christ.

steps.title: Homily
steps.text: The Book of the Gospels is taken to the credence table or another fitting place. The Priest gives the Homily at the chair or the ambo; a Deacon may give it instead. A brief period of silence is then fitting.

steps.title: Profession of Faith
steps.text: On Sundays and solemnities the Creed is sung or said. At the words about the Incarnation all bow. On the Annunciation and on Christmas all genuflect.
say: …and by the Holy Spirit was incarnate of the Virgin Mary, and became man.  (all bow)
…and the life of the world to come. Amen.

steps.title: Universal Prayer (Prayer of the Faithful)
steps.text: Standing at the chair, the Priest introduces the prayer with hands joined. The Deacon, or a cantor, lector or lay person, announces the intentions from the ambo, and the people respond. The Priest ends with a prayer, his hands extended.

steps.title: Preparation of the Altar
steps.text: The Offertory Chant begins. The Deacon and ministers bring the corporal, purificator, chalice, pall and Missal from the credence table and place them on the altar.

steps.title: Presentation of the Gifts
steps.text: It is praiseworthy for the faithful to present the bread and wine. The Priest or the Deacon receives them at a suitable place and carries them to the altar.

steps.title: Offering of the Bread and Wine
steps.text: At the altar the Priest holds the paten with the bread slightly raised and says the prayer of blessing in a low voice. The Deacon pours wine and a little water into the chalice while the Priest prays quietly. The Priest holds the chalice slightly raised, says the second prayer and places it on the corporal. If there is no singing, the people may respond aloud. The Priest then bows profoundly and prays quietly.

D: pours wine and a little water

say: (low voice) Blessed are you, Lord God of all creation…
(quietly) By the mystery of this water and wine may we come to share in the divinity of Christ who humbled himself to share in our humanity.
(low voice) Blessed are you… fruit of the vine…

steps.title: Incensing the Gifts, Altar, Priest and People
steps.text: If appropriate, the Priest incenses the offerings, the cross and the altar. Then the Deacon or another minister incenses the Priest and the people.

steps.title: Washing of Hands
steps.text: Standing at the side of the altar, the Priest washes his hands, saying a prayer quietly.
say: (quietly) Wash me, O Lord, from my iniquity and cleanse me from my sin.

steps.title: "Pray, brethren" & Prayer over the Offerings
steps.text: Back at the middle of the altar and facing the people, the Priest extends and then joins his hands and says "Pray, brethren". The people rise and reply. With hands extended, the Priest then says the Prayer over the Offerings, and the people acclaim "Amen."
say: Pray, brethren, that my sacrifice and yours may be acceptable to God, the almighty Father.
May the Lord accept the sacrifice at your hands for the praise and glory of his name, for our good and the good of all his holy Church.

steps.title: Eucharistic Prayer: Preface Dialogue & Preface
steps.text: The Eucharistic Prayer begins. With hands extended, the Priest sings or says the opening dialogue, raising his hands at "Lift up your hearts." He then continues the Preface with hands extended.
say: We lift them up to the Lord.
Let us give thanks to the Lord our God.

steps.title: Sanctus
steps.text: At the end of the Preface the Priest joins his hands. Together with the people he concludes it by singing or saying the Sanctus aloud. The ministers take their places to kneel for the consecration.
say: ♪ Holy, Holy, Holy Lord God of hosts… Hosanna in the highest. ♪

steps.title: Epiclesis
steps.text: After the Sanctus the people kneel, where this is the custom. The Deacon kneels from the epiclesis until the chalice is shown. The Priest holds his hands extended over the offerings and calls down the Holy Spirit. He then joins his hands and makes the Sign of the Cross over the bread and chalice together. Shortly before the consecration a minister may ring a small bell as a signal.

P: makes the Sign of the Cross over them ✠

say: (calls down the Holy Spirit upon the gifts) …that they may become for us the Body and ✠ Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ.

steps.title: Consecration: the Host
steps.text: The words of the Lord are spoken clearly and distinctly. The Priest takes the bread, holds it slightly raised above the altar and bows slightly as he says the words of Institution. He shows the consecrated host to the people and places it again on the paten. Then he genuflects in adoration. The bell may be rung, and the host incensed, when it is shown to the people.

P: shows the Host to the people

say: …TAKE THIS, ALL OF YOU, AND EAT OF IT, FOR THIS IS MY BODY, WHICH WILL BE GIVEN UP FOR YOU.

steps.title: Consecration: the Chalice
steps.text: In the same way the Priest takes the chalice and says the words over it. He shows the chalice to the people, places it on the corporal and genuflects in adoration. The bell may be rung and incense offered as before.

P: shows the Chalice to the people

say: …TAKE THIS, ALL OF YOU, AND DRINK FROM IT, FOR THIS IS THE CHALICE OF MY BLOOD…  DO THIS IN MEMORY OF ME.

steps.title: The Mystery of Faith
steps.text: The Priest says "The mystery of faith," and the people respond with one of the acclamations. The Deacon rises.
say: We proclaim your Death, O Lord, and profess your Resurrection until you come again.

steps.title: Memorial, Offering & Intercessions
steps.text: With hands extended, the Priest continues the Eucharistic Prayer. The Church keeps the memorial of Christ, offers the spotless Victim and prays for communion in the Holy Spirit. It intercedes for the whole Church, for the living and the dead, and recalls the saints.
say: (memorial and offering… for the Pope, the Bishop, all the clergy… for those who have died… with the Blessed Virgin Mary and all the Saints…)

steps.title: Concluding Doxology
steps.text: The Priest takes the paten with the host, and the Deacon takes the chalice, and they raise them together. The Priest alone sings or says the doxology, and the people acclaim "Amen."

P: raises the paten with the Host

say: Through him, and with him, and in him, O God, almighty Father, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, all glory and honor is yours, for ever and ever.

steps.title: The Lord's Prayer
steps.text: With hands joined, the Priest introduces the Lord's Prayer. With hands extended, he says it together with the people. He alone adds the embolism, "Deliver us, Lord…", and the people conclude it with the acclamation.
say: At the Savior's command and formed by divine teaching, we dare to say:
Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name…
Deliver us, Lord, we pray, from every evil…
For the kingdom, the power and the glory are yours now and for ever.

steps.title: Rite of Peace
steps.text: With hands extended, the Priest says the prayer for peace. Facing the people, he says "The peace of the Lord be with you always." If appropriate, the Deacon invites all to offer a sign of peace. The Priest gives the sign of peace to the Deacon or a minister and stays within the sanctuary.

P: sign of peace to the Deacon

say: Lord Jesus Christ, who said to your Apostles: Peace I leave you…
The peace of the Lord be with you always.
Let us offer each other the sign of peace.
(the faithful exchange a sign of peace)

steps.title: Fraction of the Bread — Agnus Dei
steps.text: The Priest breaks the host over the paten and places a small piece in the chalice, saying a prayer quietly. Meanwhile the Agnus Dei is sung or said. In many places the faithful kneel after it.

P: places a particle in the chalice

say: (quietly) May this mingling of the Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ bring eternal life to us who receive it.
♪ Lamb of God, you take away the sins of the world… grant us peace. ♪

steps.title: "Behold the Lamb of God"
steps.text: With hands joined, the Priest quietly says the prayer before Communion. He genuflects, takes the host and holds it slightly raised above the paten or chalice. Facing the people, he says "Behold the Lamb of God…" and then says "Lord, I am not worthy…" once, together with the people.
say: Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who takes away the sins of the world. Blessed are those called to the supper of the Lamb.
Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof, but only say the word and my soul shall be healed.

steps.title: Holy Communion
steps.text: Facing the altar, the Priest says a prayer quietly and reverently receives the Body of Christ, then the Blood. He gives Communion to the Deacon and ministers. The faithful then approach in procession. Showing each a host slightly raised, he says "The Body of Christ," and the communicant replies "Amen." Meanwhile the Communion Chant is sung.
say: (quietly) May the Body of Christ keep me safe for eternal life.

steps.title: Purification & Sacred Silence
steps.text: When Communion is over, the Deacon (or the Priest) consumes any of the Blood that remains, and the hosts that remain are placed in the tabernacle. The sacred vessels are purified at the credence table or the altar. The Priest returns to the chair. A period of sacred silence may follow, or a psalm or hymn of praise may be sung.

steps.title: Prayer after Communion
steps.text: Standing at the chair or the altar, the Priest says "Let us pray" and then, with hands extended, the Prayer after Communion. The people acclaim "Amen."

steps.title: Greeting & Blessing
steps.text: Brief announcements may be made if necessary. The Priest extends his hands and greets the people, then blesses them. On some days a Solemn Blessing or a Prayer over the People is used, and the Deacon may invite all to bow down for the blessing.
say: May almighty God bless you, the Father, and the Son, ✠ and the Holy Spirit.

steps.title: Dismissal & Veneration of the Altar
steps.text: With hands joined and facing the people, the Deacon dismisses them, and the people reply. The Priest and Deacon then venerate the altar with a kiss as at the beginning.
say: Go forth, the Mass is ended.

steps.title: Recession
steps.text: After a profound bow with the ministers, the Priest leaves with them, in much the same way as the entrance procession.
